rv.q: It’s an impressive piece of solo performance, and, whenever you go, you’re guaranteed to get something you didn’t expect.

But the flaw in his soft-liberal approach, which implies a moral equivalence between all forms of protest, is that it comes dangerously close to Trumpism and I can’t believe that is what Drummond would wish.
It’s all suitably entertaining, for sure, but I’m not sure it sparks as much debate as it could.
Well, it's well staged, the performer is engaging and the keypads are fun, it's never boring but I'm not convinced it adds up to much more than that.

cn.t: Rob Drummond's interactive voting play tackles timely ethical questions through audience participation, but critics find its binary choices overly simplistic despite slick staging and relevant post-referendum themes.
